correctness.rationale: Cai et al.'s Type-A characterization applies because two distinct equal-weight words differ in at least two positions. It also has a direct proof here: with first/last differences L<R, any common read made by deleting at i in x and j in y with i<j must satisfy i≤L<R≤j and y_m=x_{m+1} for i≤m<j. Before L both words agree, so x_i through x_L are constant and all alignments of this orientation give the same read. The other orientation similarly gives at most one. Both are needed for two distinct reads, and together force opposing alternating phases throughout [L,R]; conversely the two end alignments of such an interval give distinct reads. Fixed weight forces an even length 2t, and the one-position sum changes by ±t with 1≤t≤r, hence separates every edge modulo r+1. The proposed r+1 words have opposite phases on exactly the indicated even interval for each pair; complementing and padding cover unbalanced layers and r=0 is a singleton. The base five words have the cyclic pair intersection sizes 2 and the other five intersection sizes 0; padding preserves the differing interval, so the induced obstruction persists in every stated layer. An independent enumerator compared the interval criterion, residue and actual distinct deletion sets for 32,587 pairs through n=9 and computed all ten witness intersections (`python3 /workspace/review_checks.py 4`). The general proof does not depend on the finite census.
residual_risks: Induced C₅ is proved in the stated range, not asserted to be absent outside it. No exact largest color class or independence number is deduced.

evidence: Theorem 17 uses inversion mod 1+P/2 for even P, a symbol-sum syndrome and a bound P on period-two substrings. Its proof uses precisely the inversion difference t for an even flip of length 2t.

In a balanced layer P=2r already admits every word, so the prior theorem supplies this upper bound there. In unbalanced layers a word can contain a period-two substring of length 2r+1; choosing P=2r need not admit the entire layer, and raising to the next even P changes the modulus. The assigned argument bounds even conflicting intervals only.

The prior unrestricted pencil construction overlaps the clique witness, but the compared clique and edge results do not supply the odd-hole witness or combine all layer bounds into the asserted classification.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the prior proof mechanism and the covered balanced coloring, rather than treating lack of identical wording as novelty. What survives is the sharp natural full-layer statement with the correct modulus also for unbalanced compositions, and the induced odd-hole statement. The broader comparisons do not imply that combined result.

checked_sources: Cai et al., Theorem 17, for the existing syndrome mechanism
value.rationale: The fixed-composition layer is a natural channel class and the minimum number of jointly reconstructible codebooks is a concrete partition cost; neither a bound on just one codebook nor edge enumeration answers it. A simple optimal syndrome and explicit sharp obstruction cover every composition, while the embedded C₅ shows that the equality is not explained by perfection. This gives a precise graph/coding distinction rather than an isolated finite instance.
residual_risks: The result is not a capacity theorem for a single codebook or a complete classification of perfect layers.
